database_snapshots.rule: most recent 3 complete versions + last 1 per UTC day for 7 days + 1 explicit baseline; duplicates count once

protected_otherwise: db-20261106T095015Z.sql.gz -> legacy record, unknown source; never a deletion candidate

database_snapshots.integrity_check: every deleted file matched its recorded sha256, its recorded size and read back as valid gzip immediately before unlink; the ledger was rewritten atomically in its native shape
database_snapshots.native_rotation_defect_found: snapshot._prune reads every recorded snapshot in the ledger and raises CutoverError if one record is incomplete; db-20261106T095015Z (legacy: bytes/created/reason, no sha256/stamp) triggers exactly that, so every automatic rotation run has been aborting and preserving all older snapshots. The retention rule was applied with the same select_retained() function offline instead. Fixing the ledger record or the prune precondition is left as a follow-up because it changes code outside this reclamation.
